card.title: Stay for the Hard Part
card.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I haven't booked our anniversary trip. Can you hear why before you get your laptop?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you just needed help with the flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I let you think that. I was relieved when the cheap seats sold out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave the laptop shut. Is it the trip, or us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Us. I hoped a cancellation would say it for me. Can you still sit beside me while I explain?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks to explain nonbooking, A3 admits relief at lost cheap seats and A5 admits hoping cancellation would express doubt about us.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 flight-help assumption causes A3 acknowledgment of letting it stand; B4 laptop shut and trip-or-us question cause A5 deeper truth.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers practical help and B4 changes to attentive listening while asking a direct clarifying question.

heightening.evidence: B4 continued presence permits A5 the hardest admission and an explicit request to remain beside A through it.

specificity.evidence: A1 anniversary trip and B2 laptop help establish the visible problem and its hidden emotional layer.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 cancellation speaking for A makes the avoidance concrete; wit remains restrained.
